issue: LAMBDA_COST is mis-calibrated by a double-counted i0 in src/calibrate.py
status: RESOLVED. The fix was applied to src/model.py and src/calibrate.py by a teammate at ~03:06 (model.py sha1 1e28a351fcd6277d738a44162fda62d9542d04d3, LAMBDA_COST = 0.009827704). results/cells.csv and results/npe_meta.json were re-run WITHOUT --lam so they are self-consistent with the official constant; the re-run is numerically identical to the --lam=0.00982770365058944 run (max abs diff 5e-4, one discrete ppf_control cell).

evidence.calibrate_py_code: neutral_lambda(): burden0 = TH[:,5] * PA[:,0]; return median(burden0)/TAU.max()
evidence.why_buggy: PA[:,0] = cumulative_incidence(theta, beta_scale) is ALREADY proportional to i0 (it is the per-capita burden). Multiplying by TH[:,5] again double-counts the seed. The declared rule median(i0*Phi_0)/tau_max needs Phi_0 = the seed-amplification factor (= burden / i0), not the burden itself.

consequence_of_the_bug.note: With lambda=8.67e-8 the cost term is ~1e-8 while the burden margin is ~5.6e-3, so the burden term dominates for EVERY parameter in the prior.
consequence_of_the_bug.verdict: decision fully degenerate (always choose maximal coverage tau=0.60); PPF identically 0; the paper's mechanism (a decision that flips across the rho-i0 ridge) cannot operate.

decision_after_correction.verdict: non-degenerate; all three tiers are optimal for a substantial share of the prior.

suggested_one_line_fix_in_calibrate_py: return float(np.median(PA[:, 0]) / TAU.max())   # drop the TH[:,5] factor
fraction_grid_note: results/cells.csv (canonical) uses the corrected lambda; results/cells_lambda_model.csv preserves the original (degenerate) run for the record.
